html:
Here is an image of the Cocoon Nebula with the open cluster IC5146.

In fact, three objects are combined in this portion of the sky in the constellation Cygnus to form this particular view. These three objects are:

1- The Cocoon Nebula (Sh 2-125 in the Sharpless catalog) is a reflection/emission nebula. That is, it emits part of its light and another part comes from the reflection of the light of the nearby group of stars. Its red color comes from hydrogen excited by the young stars of the cluster.

2- The open cluster IC 5146, also designated number 19 in the Caldwell catalog. It is the group of stars located at the center of the nebula. Its age is about 100,000 years.

3- The dark nebula Barnard 168. It is the dark band that starts near the nebula and extends to the right of the photo. This opaque cloud blocks the light of the stars behind it.

The nebula has a diameter of 15 light-years and is located 4000 light-years from earth.


Technical details
Date: 2009-10-16
Temperature: 0 to -5 degrees celsius.
Telescope: Takahashi SKY90 II with dedicated f 4.5 focal reducer (407mm focal length)
Sensor: Canon 40D unfiltered
Filter: IDAS-LPS (to counter light pollution)
Mount: LX200 10" f 6.3 classic
Guiding: QHY5 and PHD

40 frames of 300 seconds (1 rejected because of the factory smoke), 40 darks, 40 flats
Calibrated and stacked in DeepSkyStacker
Processing in photoshop
